claims.text: The rider's claim is that a short hop became 3.96 km and $9.64. The governing distance is the trace figure, and the trace records 3.96 km against a booked optimal of 3.2 km — an excess of 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of optimal. The percentage test under POL-RD-01 is met (23.75% > 20%), so the first limb of the establishment test passes on the rider's own evidence.

The second limb of the POL-RD-01 establishment test fails: the excess of 0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. Both tests must pass, and one does not. On the trace as measured, no route deviation is ESTABLISHED, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. I concede this point — the arithmetic does not support a deviation finding on this record.

The driver's explanation for the route is 'One-way streets.' That is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle holds no advisory covering the Jurong Point corridor in this window — the artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 — so the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver's excuse does not reduce the measured excess or supply an amended optimal.

The driver's traffic assertion cites no evidence ID for an advisory. Under POL-RD-13(1), an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. The missing advisory is therefore not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger on these facts.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 45 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and no straight-line jump over 500 m. It does not meet any of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The rider's claim is not defeated by a data failure.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges limb (a): the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02843 and the same pickup timestamp of 2026-08-18T06:30:45+08:00. The artifacts describe the same trip.

The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so no additional corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required for a claim with excess below 30%. The rider's claim is not burdened by a pattern of unsubstantiated claims.

The fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The rider has paid $9.64 and received nothing back. If the tribunal finds any refund is due, the present state leaves the rider carrying the full disputed charge.

The fare_breakdown shows no ERP gantries charged and no airport surcharge, so there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) and no pass-through correction available on this record. I do not assert one.

The chat_log carries zero messages. There is no rider instruction in the chat_log that could exonerate any part of the route under POL-RD-04, and no rider-requested detour to exclude from the excess. The driver cannot rely on a chat-based excuse on this record.

The driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 and completed_trips_90d of 228. That is below the POL-RD-06 pattern threshold of 3 flags, and 1/228 is far below the 0.05 ratio. No repeat deviation pattern is established, and I do not assert one.

The trip_record shows no amendment to pickup or dropoff: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-05 cannot be run and does not apply. The booked optimal of 3.2 km stands as the baseline.
The vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline is not in play. The solo optimal of 3.2 km is the correct baseline for the POL-RD-01 test.
The fare_model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE, and quoted_fare_sgd is null. POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route on this trip; POL-RD-02 would run if a deviation were established.

The rider's claim is that the trip was too long and too expensive. On the trace as measured, the excess of 0.76 km fails the absolute threshold of 0.8 km under POL-RD-01, so no deviation is established and no refund is available under POL-RD-02. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence, and the present state stands. I concede the monetary outcome on this record.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the $9.64 charge stands exactly as it is. No refund is paid to the rider and no compensation is paid to the driver.

The route-deviation test in POL-RD-01 is conjunctive, and that is what decides this case. A deviation is established only if the distance driven exceeds the booked optimal route by more than 20% AND by more than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The governing distance is the GPS trace figure, because POL-RD-01 says the trace governs and the trip-record copy (4.0 km) is a rounded convenience value that may not be cited for the threshold. On the trace, the trip ran 3.96 km against a booked optimal of 3.2 km, an excess of 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of optimal. The percentage limb passes (23.75% > 20%), but the absolute limb fails: 0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km. Both limbs must pass, so no deviation is established on this trip's own measurement, and POL-RD-02 (the optimal-route fare recomputation) never runs. The fare sheet's own arithmetic would have produced a $0.96 refund (payable $1.00) had a deviation been established, but that figure is gated behind POL-RD-01 and moves no money here. Both facts that decide the case — the trace distance and the booked optimal — come from artifacts carried at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-02843 and EV-TRIP-02843), so the confidence cap is 1.0.

I checked every other route to a refund, and none is open. The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 45 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so no data failure is held against the rider and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) arises. The fare ledger reconciles — base fare $3.80, distance $3.00 on 4.0 charged km at $0.75/km, time $2.04 on 7.3 charged minutes at $0.28/min, platform fee $0.80, no ERP lines and no surcharges, totalling $9.64 — so there is no phantom gantry and no misplaced airport surcharge to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The chat log holds zero messages, so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 can be made out; the trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, so POL-RD-05 relocation does not apply and the 3.2 km booked optimal stands; the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is not in play; and the fare model is METERED with no quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 neither closes nor changes the arithmetic.

The profile checks were run and both came back below their thresholds. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 228 — below the POL-RD-06 pattern threshold of 3 flags or a 0.05 ratio — so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no conduct referral and no refund uplift follow. The rider's deviation_claims_60d is 1 with 0 substantiated, below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so no extra corroboration beyond the trace was required of the rider's claim; the claim simply does not clear the 0.8 km absolute limb.

The driver's explanation in the case file ('One-way streets') was not needed and is not weighed: because no deviation was established, the route needs no excuse, and in any event no traffic advisory was on file for this trip. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires — the timestamps and trip identifiers agree, the trace is not impaired, both parties agree on the arithmetic, and no charge line lacks a counterpart.

Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands: the $9.64 charge and the zero refund_issued_sgd are left as they are. No referral is made, because no clause produces one on these facts (POL-RD-06(c) needs a material deviation plus a pattern; POL-RD-09(4) needs a billing-integrity defect; neither exists here). The monetary effect of this ruling is nil, which is below the automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the rider's claim fails on the POL-RD-01 threshold, so the $9.64 charge stands and no money moves.

The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02843), which records 3.96 km against a booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02843) of 3.2 km. The excess is 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of optimal. POL-RD-01 makes the establishment test conjunctive: the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The percentage limb passes (23.75% > 20%); the absolute limb fails, because 0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km. No route deviation is established on this trip's own trace, so POL-RD-02 never runs — the money block's $0.96 figure, rounded up to $1.00, is never reached.

The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 45 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, with no jump over 500 m. It is not impaired, so the measurement stands as recorded and no corroboration question arises. The driver's 'one-way streets' explanation is an assertion of an external traffic cause; no traffic advisory covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-02843-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight — but the outcome does not turn on it, because the claim fails on the threshold regardless.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties.

THE DISTANCE. POL-RD-01 measures the actual distance from the GPS trace, and the trace figure governs over the trip record's rounded copy. The trace (EV-GPS-02843) runs 3.96 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02843) is 3.2 km. The excess is 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of optimal.

WHY NO DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs of the establishment test to pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The percentage limb passes (23.75% > 20%). The absolute limb fails: 0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km. Because the test is conjunctive, no route deviation is established on this trip, POL-RD-02 is never reached, and no distance or time refund is available. Rider: the trip did run longer than the optimal route — 760 m, barely under the 800 m floor — but the policy sets that floor and this case sits below it. Both advocates conceded this arithmetic and I agree with both of them.

THE FARE. The $9.64 charged (EV-FARE-02843) is base fare 3.80 + distance charge 2.40 + time charge 1.68 + platform fee 0.80, with no ERP lines, no tolls and no surcharges. There is no phantom gantry and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09(4) yields no standalone billing-integrity correction. The ledger reconciles on its face.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. Driver, you said "One-way streets." POL-RD-13 tests a traffic assertion against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. The advisory artifact (EV-ADVIS-02843-01) is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT: no advisory covers the Jurong Point corridor in this window. The comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and your assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It does not change the outcome, because no deviation was established and so nothing needed exonerating; and because no advisory ID was cited, the missing advisory is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger (POL-RD-13(1)).

OTHER LIMBS CHECKED. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02843) carries 0 messages, so POL-RD-04 exonerates nothing and no rider-requested detour can be made out. The rider was billed 4.0 km against a 3.96 km trace, so no distance went unbilled and the POL-RD-04 DRIVER_COMPENSATION limb does not fire. No endpoint was amended (POL-RD-05 not available). Vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12 not applicable). The driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 228 completed trips, below both POL-RD-06 thresholds, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no uplift applies and no conduct referral follows. The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 45 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, max gap 0.0 s, no jump over 500 m, so it is not impaired and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

OUTCOME. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands. Under POL-GEN-03 this is NO_ACTION: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left exactly as they are. No refund and no driver compensation issue. The monetary effect is SGD 0.00, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so nothing is held pending review.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling decides the route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-02843 for both parties. The figures come from the GPS trace EV-GPS-02843 and the trip record EV-TRIP-02843 (both at full weight 1.0), with the money block from the fare breakdown EV-FARE-02843.

1. No route deviation is established. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH an excess greater than 20% of the booked optimal distance AND an excess greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The governing distance is the trace figure of 3.96 km, not the rounded 4.0 km convenience copy on the trip record. Measured against the booked optimal of 3.2 km, the excess is 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of optimal: the percentage gate passes, but the absolute gate fails, because 0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km. One limb failing is enough, and POL-RD-01 states that where either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION. (Even taking the trip record's rounded 4.0 km, the excess would be exactly 0.80 km — still not greater than 0.8 km.)

2. The fare is therefore left alone. POL-RD-02 recomputation applies only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, so it never runs here. The money block's conditional figures (recomputed_fare 8.68, refund_before_rounding 0.96) rest on a deviation that was not established and produce no refund. The $9.64 charged total (base fare 3.80 + distance 3.00 + time 2.04 + platform fee 0.80) stands, and payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0 is left exactly as it is — that is what NO_ACTION means on a rider-filed dispute under POL-GEN-03.

3. The driver's explanation, 'One-way streets' in the counterparty statement, is an assertion of an external traffic cause. There is no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-02843-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 that assertion is tested against the traffic advisory and nothing else, so it carries no weight and reduces no excess. It is also not an escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(5), because the driver cited no advisory identifier and an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one. In any event the excess fails the POL-RD-01 gate on its own, so nothing turns on the excuse.

4. No billing-integrity defect. The fare ledger reconciles to $9.64, there are no ERP gantry lines and no airport surcharge, and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record, so no standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4) arises and no billing-integrity referral is made. The billed 4.0 km is a rounding of the trace distance, not a phantom line.

5. No conduct referral. The driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 228 — below both the 3-flag test and the 0.05-ratio test in POL-RD-06 — so no repeat deviation pattern is established and POL-RD-06(c) does not fire. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d 1, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0) is below the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger, so no corroboration beyond the trace was required. Every other profile field is context only under POL-GEN-01 and supported no finding.

6. No escalation. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c): 45 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps (max gap 0.0 s) and no jump over 500 m. Trip identifiers and pickup timestamps agree across trip record, trace and fare breakdown. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires.

Confidence is 0.9: the deciding fact — the 0.76 km excess against the 0.8 km gate — is carried by the trace and the trip record, both at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; the absent advisory at weight 0.0 carries no fact. The monetary effect is nil, so nothing needs holding, but the ruling is provisional and either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
